cells.tense: The practice is here, and it can be shown in the doing.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Once today's session ends, set down what you did in the order it happened, moods left out. Put the page where tomorrow's work will start.
cells.core:
You can push one stubborn way of working into something that holds, and you do it by repetition rather than force. A sequence clicks into place, you run it again, and the running is what keeps it clear. Solitude in this work isn't distance from people; it's where the refinement happens, and you come back with something anyone can see. The inquiry earns its answers this way — one session, then the next.

Keep the record plain this week. After the work, put your steps down in the order they happened, without the feelings around them. Not a journal — a list. The facts are where this shows; feeling has its place, but not as proof. Then run the same sequence again tomorrow, exactly as written, and trust the doing to carry it.
cells.sheetLine: You make the practice hold by running it again.
cells.verb: forcing change into form, slow and unstoppable
cells.place: a small, steady light kept lit by repetition

cells.tense: The practice will be finished before it is shown to anyone.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Do one piece of your practice in front of another person this week. No lecture — the doing itself, and whatever comes back.
cells.core:
You're pushing the practice toward a finished form. The schedule gets tightened, the method gets weapons-grade, and the next version wants more proof before it will count. It looks focused from the inside. From the outside it's a door being built around, not opened. The inquiry is meant to produce clarity you can use with people, and right now it produces more inquiry.

The practice can leave the room it was built in.

Take one piece of it to another person this week and work it with them — the thing itself, not a report about it. Permit it to change a little in their hands. Whatever they hand back, the direction stays yours; the meaning only lives when it's shared. Very little is required, and what's done is done.

cells.tense: You had a practice once, and you are still standing where it stopped.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Lay out the tools and begin the practice once, without a plan for the whole return. Start it, and stop there if you want.
cells.core:
The practice isn't running. Whatever was built by repetition is sitting where it was left, and you're at the door with the lights off, treating the gap as the fact and the return as unavailable. The old work still exists; you can name its shape. What's missing is that anything is currently moving. Waiting for the right feeling to come back is how the door stays shut.

One act, done now, is the way through — not a plan, not a rebuild. Set the tools on the table, do the first motion. The decision is already yours to make; carry it through once, and the practice has somewhere to land. Sitting still and waiting are not the same thing here; you don't need to feel ready, only to begin.

cells.tense: The practice is building, and you're saying it happened by itself.
cells.act: hold the direction with courage, day after day
cells.ask: Keep the practice at the size it is now, no larger, and stay with that same shape through the days it gives nothing back.
cells.core:
Building things in the quiet — the early rise, the one more round, the small piece done before the day starts — and the story you tell is that it's just what's needed. The hand is on it. The results are real, and the one doing the work stands outside the frame, watching it happen as if it were not theirs. It is theirs. The persistence has hours in it.

Go back to the want. Hold the practice at the size it is now, no larger, and keep that line through the days it gives nothing back. Motivation doesn't need a bonfire; it needs the fire fed regularly. Doing it because you chose to, on the dull days, puts your name on the run of it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that in the Balanced cell a practice already 'flows without force' — the record calls that the partner's balanced character, not the person's present state. The reader's likely objection is 'I haven't found a practice that flows, I just grind on it,' which the Too Much cell would fit better; if my read is wrong, the ask (writing the sequence down in order) is still useful because it disciplines without requiring flow. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: 'The practice is already steady and the inquiries already land' — cut, because the record does not report a state, only where the capacity is seated.
